title: Maintain an Annals knowledge library
summary: Initialize, migrate, inspect, or back up the library, and explicitly apply, simplify, or revert its versioned idea map.
use_when: Library schema, backup, statistics, explicit reconciliation application, graph normalization, history, or reversion must be operated.
Strict reconciliation JSON should be submitted without a model run.
do_not_use_when: The task is ordinary source retention, model-assisted integration, corpus exploration, or inbox operation.
The proposed procedure overwrites a backup, edits internal rows, or assumes a stale pending reconciliation can be forced.
A destructive installed fresh-state cutover has not been explicitly authorized.
outcome: A deterministic library read or atomic state transition whose revision, provenance, compatibility, and recovery consequences are explicit.
effects: Initialization creates revision zero; migration upgrades only supported prior schemas; backup creates a consistent SQLite copy without replacing its destination.
Applying, shaking, or reverting creates an append-only commit and advances the corpus revision when it changes state.
Direct reconciliation submission validates a projected state but does not apply it.
authority: The Annals library and canonical reducer own all corpus state, reconciliation, commit, revision, and provenance truth.
No model or Nucleus job is required for deterministic library operations.
success: The selected command reports the exact library, revision, reconciliation, backup, statistics, or migration result.
Every mutation is atomic and the resulting library passes its relevant invariants.
A confirmed shake or revert records a new commit rather than rewriting history.
failure_and_recovery: Migration rejects unsupported old or newer schemas without partial mutation.
A pending reconciliation cannot apply after HEAD diverges from its base; re-resolve rather than force it.
Revert conflicts atomically when relevant facts changed; unrelated state remains untouched.
privacy: Library and backup files contain retained source, evidence, model-run provenance, and complete corpus history and must remain private.
Choose a private explicit backup destination and preserve its access controls.
does_not_authorize: Overwriting an existing database or backup destination.
Applying a pending reconciliation without explicit authorization.
Bypassing confirmation, stale-state, migration, or history checks.

consumers.statement: An authorized local operator or expert caller may initialize, inspect, migrate, back up, reconcile, normalize, or revert one Annals library through deterministic product-owned commands.
This capability is not ordinary source retention, model-assisted integration, inbox operation, direct row editing, or an implicit destructive fresh-state cutover.

preconditions.statement: The caller explicitly selects the target library and holds authority for the requested mutation; initialization and backup require absent destination paths.

Reconciliation application requires a valid pending result whose base is current HEAD, shake confirmation requires the exact preview context, and revert requires relevant facts not to have conflicted.

inputs.statement: Inputs select one command and library, an absent backup destination, strict reconciliation JSON with work and base revision, a pending work, or a commit revision to revert.
Arbitrary SQL, in-place backup replacement, forced stale application, unsupported-schema reinterpretation, history erasure, and bypass of confirmation are not accepted.

outputs.statement: The selected command reports the exact initialized or migrated library, statistics, backup result, reconciliation validation, shake plan or commit, revert commit, and resulting revision as applicable.

data_semantics.statement: Initialization creates revision zero; application, confirmed nonempty shake, and successful revert append a commit and advance the corpus rather than rewriting prior history.
Direct reconciliation submission resolves and validates a complete projected corpus state but does not apply it.
Shake removes only direct parent edges already implied by longer paths, preserving reachability but not every direct-neighbor count or hop distance.

identity_and_units.statement: The selected library, public cN concept IDs, normalized work labels, reconciliation identity, commit identity, and integer corpus revision are distinct selectors.
Backup paths identify filesystem copies, while statistics and shake plans report documented record and edge counts rather than usage or billing units.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Backup creates one consistent SQLite copy of the selected library, and validation re-resolves the stored request against its exact base rather than trusting a cached projection.
Every mutation checks the current library state at commit time and either applies its complete atomic transition or leaves the library unchanged.
No backup duration, maximum library size, migration latency, or long-term backup-retention guarantee is promised.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local Annals CLI operating one explicitly resolved private library and an explicitly chosen backup or request file where applicable.
Direct SQLite mutation, manual database replacement, remote administration, and model execution are not supported by this capability.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Supported migrations and all corpus mutations are transactional; failure or conflict leaves no partial transition.
Application requires unchanged base HEAD, confirmed shake binds to exact library identity and HEAD, and revert appends an inverse commit while preserving unrelated intervening facts.
Initialization and backup refuse replacement, and migration rejects unsupported older or newer schemas without partial reinterpretation.

operational_limits.statement: Migration accepts only documented prior schemas; backup and initialization never overwrite; stale reconciliation has no force path; destructive installed fresh state is outside this operation.
No maximum library, reconciliation, backup, or commit size, throughput, or wall-clock latency is promised here.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 2, provider release, library schema, reconciliation shape, and installed package generation are distinct; migrations cover only explicitly supported prior schemas.
Revert and commit history are append-only compatibility records; older history is not rewritten to current meaning.
No universal forward-compatibility, migration window, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Deterministic library operations invoke no Nucleus, model, network, or other product; filesystem storage is inside the selected Annals operating boundary.
